status_policy: The rule is an empirical model fitted on the empirical opcode map. It is not an independent native proof; a predicted opcode must still be compatible with the operand shape of its PHP 5.2 handler before it is decoded.

derivation.note: Every empirical key is reproduced; a byte seen at several positions yields one base.

independent_cross_check.note: The archived trace audit is not an independent proof of the Encoder format. The key 1:199 has no archived candidate at all, because the runtime trace of that file carries an extra instruction at that position; the rule therefore predicts it without contradicting the archive.

disputed_keys.note: The position rule reproduces 140 for these keys, but the native meaning of 140 stays unresolved; the Encoder level call semantics is handled by encoder_call_map.json.

limitations: The rule is fitted on the empirical map; it adds predictions, not new native observations.
Only bytes present in the byte base table can be predicted.
A negative prediction is refused instead of wrapped around.
The native semantics of a predicted opcode is not established by the rule itself.
